title: “All conditioned things are impermanent” — When one sees this with wisdom, One becomes disenchanted with suffering — This is the path to purity. “All…
content:
“All conditioned things are impermanent” —
When one sees this with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

“All conditioned things are suffering” —
When one sees this with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

“All phenomena are not-self” —
When one sees this with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

title: Behold this decorated image — A heap of wounds, a collection of sores, Diseased, the object of many lustful thoughts, Nothing stable or permanent here.
content:
Behold this decorated image —
A heap of wounds, a collection of sores,
Diseased, the object of many lustful thoughts,
Nothing stable or permanent here.

title: “I do not see any other sound, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the sound of a woman. The…
content: “I do not see any other sound, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the sound of a woman. The sound of a woman, monks, obsesses and occupies the mind of a man.”

title: “Along with this suffering, abandon sensual desires, Seeking future security from bondage. Rightly understanding, with mind well liberated, There, right there, one is liberated from…
content:
“Along with this suffering, abandon sensual desires,
Seeking future security from bondage.
Rightly understanding, with mind well liberated,
There, right there, one is liberated from contact.
That one attains knowledge,
Accomplishes the holy life,
Reaches the end of the world,
Gets to the far shore —
That one is so called.”

title: “Monks, what is non-clinging and non-worry? Here, monks, a well-taught noble disciple regards form as: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is…
content: “Monks, what is non-clinging and non-worry? Here, monks, a well-taught noble disciple regards form as: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ For him, that form changes and alters. When form changes and alters, no sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, or despair arise in him. He regards feeling … perception … formations … consciousness as: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ For him, that consciousness changes and alters. When consciousness changes and alters, no sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, or despair arise in him. Thus, monks, is non-clinging and non-worry.”

title: “There are these two extremes that one who has gone forth should not pursue: devotion to sensual pleasure in sensual objects — low, vulgar, worldly,…
content:
“There are these two extremes that one who has gone forth should not pursue: devotion to sensual pleasure in sensual objects — low, vulgar, worldly, ignoble, unbeneficial; and devotion to self-mortification — painful, ignoble, unbeneficial. Avoiding these two extremes, the Middle Way has been realized by the Tathāgata, giving rise to vision, giving rise to knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna.

And what, headman, is that Middle Way realized by the Tathāgata, giving rise to vision, giving rise to knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. This, headman, is the Middle Way realized by the Tathāgata, giving rise to vision, giving rise to knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna.”

title: Seclusion is happiness For one who knows contentment, For one who has heard the Dhamma, For one who sees rightly. Non-ill-will is happiness For those…
content:
Seclusion is happiness
For one who knows contentment,
For one who has heard the Dhamma,
For one who sees rightly.

Non-ill-will is happiness
For those in the world
Who practice self-restraint
Toward living beings.

Dispassion is happiness
For those who transcend sensual pleasures,
Who subdue the conceit ‘I am’ —
This is the highest happiness.

title: “For a monk practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, this is in accordance with the Dhamma: he dwells often in disenchantment toward form,…
content: “For a monk practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, this is in accordance with the Dhamma: he dwells often in disenchantment toward form, toward feeling, toward perception, toward formations, toward consciousness. Dwelling often in disenchantment toward form … toward consciousness, he fully understands form … feeling … perception … formations … consciousness. By fully understanding them, he is freed from form, freed from feeling, freed from perception, freed from formations, freed from consciousness, freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is freed from suffering.”

title: The feet are painted with lac and dye, The face is smeared with powder and paste — Enough to fool a fool, But not one…
content:
The feet are painted with lac and dye,
The face is smeared with powder and paste —
Enough to fool a fool,
But not one who seeks the far shore.

title: “Monks, shrouded by ignorance and bound by craving, this body of the fool is generated. That ignorance the fool has not abandoned. That craving the…
content: “Monks, shrouded by ignorance and bound by craving, this body of the fool is generated. That ignorance the fool has not abandoned. That craving the fool has not destroyed. Why is that? Monks, the fool does not live the holy life for the complete destruction of suffering. Therefore, with the breakup of the body, after death, the fool goes to another body. Having gone to another body, he is not freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is not freed from suffering.”
